glosses: past passive perfective participle of прорва́ть (prorvátʹ)
страд. прич. прош. вр. от прорвать

examples.text: Вся обшивка была прорвана, набивка выброшена на пол, и пружины высовывались, как готовящиеся к укусу змеи.
А Шавка цела и так же лает сипло, и одно ухо так же прорвано, и репейники в хвосте, как быть следует.
Курточка прорвана, постоянно голоден, товарищи смеются и поколачивают его…
Аннушка уже дремала, держа красный мешочек на коленах широкими руками в перчатках, из которых одна была прорвана.

glosses: адъектив. изношенный до дыр, протёртый насквозь; рваный, дырявый

examples.text: Сидя в автомобиле, он поджимал левую ногу, скрывая прорванный ботинок, из. которого смотрел большой палец.

glosses: статив., перен. не способный больше противостоять, сопротивляться какой-либо силе, сдерживать что-либо

examples.text: Господа, в то время как мы здесь разговариваем, под Красноставом происходит кровопролитное сражение, куда в наш прорванный фронт брошена наша гвардия.
Он сам не может знать хорошенько собственные дела, и в случае серьезного замешательства всё состояние может уплыть, как вода через прорванную плотину.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see break, through.
To gain popularity.

examples.text: We are in a drought of famous influencers, and it may be here to stay. People just aren’t breaking through online the way they used to, becoming household names and garnering real, mainstream fame.

glosses: To penetrate the defence of the opposition.

examples.text: Montenegro gave Wales a scare in the first minute at the Cardiff City Stadium when Stevan Jovetic broke through, only to screw his shot well wide.

glosses: To make or force a way through (a barrier)
Partizip Perfekt des Verbs durchbrechen
Qui a un trou ou des trous.
Se dit d'un meuble dans lequel un autre (généralement une flèche, une lance…) est planté.

examples.text: D’azur au Saint Sébastien de carnation nimbé d’or et percé de cinq flèches du même, qui est de Mittelschaeffolsheim → voir illustration « saint percé »

glosses: Se dit d'une pièce ou un meuble présentant un ou plusieurs trous permettant de voir le champ au travers. S’applique également aux pièces et meubles dans lesquels un ou plusieurs orifices sont présents et permettent de voir une autre pièce ou meuble (à ne pas confondre avec la notion de chargé).

examples.text: D’argent au château de trois tours d’azur, ouvert et ajouré du champ, surmonté d’une moucheture d’hermine de sable, qui est de Villebret → voir illustration « bouton percé »
D’or au mont de sinople percé d’une grotte de sable mouvant de la pointe, accompagné en chef d’une colombe volante d’azur → voir illustration « mont percé d'une grotte »

glosses: Participe passé masculin singulier de percer.

examples.text: 'Sergent fut prêt : prenant des conseils auprès de la station piscicole du Service de la pêche, surfant sur Internet et surtout bricolant le dispositif de base pour la reproduction des alevines – une boîte à biscuit métallique (à l’effigie du Pape Jean XXIII), dans laquelle il a inséré une claie en plastique avec des baguettes de verre et percé des trous, pour que l’eau puisse s’écouler du bas vers le haut. — (Catherine Mougenot, Prendre soin de la nature ordinaire, 2013, page 126)

translations.source_sense_description: изношенный до дыр, протёртый насквозь; рваный, дырявый

glosses: To rend (a solid material) by holding or restraining in two places and pulling apart, whether intentionally or not; to destroy or separate.

examples.text: He tore his coat on the nail.

Then there came a reg'lar terror of a sou'wester same as you don't get one summer in a thousand, and blowed the shanty flat and ripped about half of the weir poles out of the sand. We spent consider'ble money getting 'em reset, and then a swordfish got into the pound and tore the nets all to slathers, right in the middle of the squiteague season.
He suffered, poor man, at seeing her so badly dressed, with laceless boots, and the arm-holes of her pinafore torn down to the hips; for the charwoman took no care of her.

glosses: To injure as if by pulling apart.

examples.text: He tore some muscles in a weight-lifting accident.

glosses: To destroy or reduce abstract unity or coherence, such as social, political or emotional.

examples.text: He was torn by conflicting emotions.

glosses: To make (an opening) with force or energy.

examples.text: A piece of debris tore a tiny straight channel through the satellite.
His boss will tear him a new one when he finds out.
The artillery tore a gap in the line.

glosses: To remove by tearing, or with sudden great force.

examples.text: Tear the coupon out of the newspaper.
[A] surge of muddy water tore him free from his sandy nook and tumbled him down the gully.

glosses: To demolish.

examples.text: The slums were torn down to make way for the new development.

glosses: To become torn, especially accidentally.

examples.text: My dress has torn.

glosses: To move or act with great speed, energy, or violence.

examples.text: He went tearing down the hill at 90 miles per hour.
The tornado lingered, tearing through town, leaving nothing upright.
He tore into the backlog of complaints.
I waited to hear no more, but tore up the village to find Poirot.
I've been tearing around in my fucking nightgown. 24/7 Sylvia Plath.

glosses: To smash or enter something with great force.

examples.text: The chain shot tore into the approaching line of infantry.

glosses: To be interrupted midway through.

examples.text: torn write

glosses: A hole or break caused by tearing.

examples.text: A small tear is easy to mend, if it is on the seam.

glosses: A rampage.

examples.text: to go on a tear

glosses: A drop of clear, salty liquid produced from the eyes by crying or irritation.

examples.text: Big tears streamed from Lisa's eyes, rolling down her cheeks.
Ryan wiped the tear from the paper he was crying on.

I pray you in your Letters, / When you ſhall theſe vnluckie deeds relate, / Speake of me, as I am. […] / Of one, whoſe ſubdu'd Eyes, / Albeit un-vsed to the melting moode, / Drops teares as faſt as the Arabian Trees / Their Medicinable gumme.

'[…] I remember a lady coming to inspect St. Mary's Home where I was brought up and seeing us all in our lovely Elizabethan uniforms we were so proud of, and bursting into tears all over us because "it was wicked to dress us like charity children".[…]'

glosses: Something in the form of a transparent drop of fluid matter; also, a solid, transparent, tear-shaped drop, as of some balsams or resins.

examples.text: Let Araby extol her happy coast, / Her fragrant flowers, her trees with precious tears.

glosses: A partially vitrified bit of clay in glass.
That which causes or accompanies tears; a lament; a dirge.

examples.text: Without meed of some melodious tear. Begin then, Sisters of the sacred well [...]

glosses: To produce tears.

examples.text: Her eyes began to tear in the harsh wind.
